observations: Three photos show a black electronic keyboard with white and black keys, placed on an orange plastic chair.
The keyboard has a central control panel with a small display, buttons, and a dial.
The keys appear to be standard piano-style, with 61 keys visible in the photos.
The keyboard has a purple and teal color scheme on the control panel area.
The brand 'YAMAHA' is visible in white letters on the top and side of the keyboard in all photos.
The keyboard is not powered on; no sound is heard in the photos.
The background shows a concrete wall and floor, suggesting an outdoor or semi-outdoor setting.
Watermark 'LUCKY SOUNDS SERVICES LTD' is present on all photos.

claims.evidence: The brand 'Yamaha' is visible in all photos, but there is no visual evidence to confirm it is a 'professional' model. The photos show a standard 61-key keyboard, which is common in entry-level to mid-range models.

risks.risk: The keyboard may not be functional (e.g., keys do not respond, no sound output).
risks.proof: A video clip showing the keyboard powered on, with keys being pressed and sound being produced.

risks.risk: The keyboard may have internal damage or wear not visible in photos (e.g., cracked circuit board, dead keys).
risks.proof: A close-up video of the keys being pressed and the display responding, along with a shot of the back panel showing no visible damage.

risks.risk: The keyboard may be missing accessories (e.g., power adapter, sustain pedal, stand).
risks.proof: A photo showing all included accessories laid out next to the keyboard.

proof_requests: Video of the keyboard powered on and playing a note to confirm functionality.
Close-up video of the back panel and any ports to check for damage or wear.
Photo of all included accessories (power adapter, stand, etc.).
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
